subject: Request: onward-transfer approval and encryption key custody flow for payment integrator
messages_1_subject: Vendor roster and encryption key custody details
messages_1_body:
Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to consolidate a couple of items we need to close the procurement checklist for the payment integration: 

1) Full vendor roster for any subprocessors that will see or persist EU personal data (names, primary function, processing location).
2) A short diagram and explanation of how encryption keys are managed for payment payloads — specifically whether keys are customer-owned, split-custody, or fully managed by Redwood.
3) Confirmation on whether any downstream partners (analytics, fraud scoring, backups) will receive payment-related PII and where that data may be stored (region).

I've attached our working roster template — please fill the first two columns and return. If you prefer, a short call with your security engineer would help.

Best,
Ana Ribeiro
Head of Procurement, BlueFin Payments
[Attachment: vendor_roster_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 42KB)]
messages_2_subject: Re: Vendor roster and encryption key custody details
messages_2_body:
Ana — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (infra) so we can turn this around quickly. Quick answers up front: 

- We will populate the roster and return the spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow.
- Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations) and fully-managed keys. For hosted integrations we default to managed keys but we can offer a split custody model where customer holds the master KMS key and Redwood holds ephemeral application keys. I attached a high-level diagram and redlined DPA with proposed language for BYOK and split custody.

Karthik — can you confirm the storage/forwarding behavior for our payment pipeline and flag any subprocessors that will receive raw payment PII? Please reply and include short notes for Ana's roster columns: "processor", "function", "location", "stores_pii?"

Thanks — Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redlined_dpa_20270418.pdf, encryption_key_flow_diagram.png]

messages_3_subject: Re: Vendor roster and encryption key custody details (technical details)
messages_3_body:
Marcus / team — technical details below to include in the reply to BlueFin: 

- Dataflow: Payment payloads enter the API gateway (EU region) -> transient in-memory processing on GPU hosts -> tokenized payload stored in short-term KV cache (TTL 6 hours) for retry/connectivity scenarios -> persisted in encrypted blob storage only when explicitly requested by customer (opt-in archival).
- Subprocessors that touch raw payloads: 
  * LogStream Analytics (eu-analytics.redwood.partner) — supports aggregated fraud metrics; does NOT persist raw PAN/PII by default (we redact).
  * MetricsStore (backup partner) — receives encrypted blobs for backups; blobs encrypted with application keys, keys are rotated monthly.
  * FraudAI (third-party fraud scoring) — receives tokenized payloads; may persist hashed identifiers for scoring.
- Key custody models supported: 
  1) Managed: Redwood KMS holds application master keys, we rotate and manage lifecycle.
  2) BYOK (customer-owned root): Customer imports root into their KMS; we use envelope encryption with customer root to unwrap data keys.
  3) Split custody (recommended for payments): Customer holds master key split across HSM and escrow with third-party key custodian; Redwood holds short-lived application keys only.

Practical notes for the roster: mark LogStream Analytics and MetricsStore as processors that will see encrypted or redacted data but not raw PANs under default config. FraudAI may see hashed identifiers and should be marked as "stores_pii? No (hashed)" unless BlueFin requests raw persistence.

I also approve the DPA redline changes around key-management clauses; legal can sign off on our side once BlueFin confirms which custody model they need.

- Karthik

messages_4_subject: Consolidated roster + key custody options — request for approval
messages_4_body:
Hi Ana / BlueFin team,

Thanks for the patience — attached is the completed vendor roster with our notes, plus a short diagram that shows the proposed split-custody flow if BlueFin elects that model. Highlights: 

- Vendor roster (attached): LogStream Analytics (EU), MetricsStore Backup (EU), FraudAI Ltd (EU). Columns filled: processor / function / primary region / stores_pii (Yes/No/Hashed).
- Recommended default: split custody (customer root + Redwood ephemeral keys). This gives you the strongest assurance that raw unencrypted payloads are only accessible during transient processing windows and cannot be decrypted outside of a customer-authorized session.
- DPA redlines: we included clear language for onward transfer permissions (we request permission to use the listed subprocessors and to engage additional EU-region processors for scaling; any non-EU onward transfer would require prior written consent).

Next steps we propose: 
1) Please confirm which key custody model you prefer (Managed | BYOK | Split custody) by EOD 2027-04-22.
2) If split custody is chosen, BlueFin security should complete a short key escrow questionnaire (we can host) and sign the DPA redlines.
3) If any processor on the roster is unacceptable, flag them and we will propose alternates.

Attachments included: vendor_roster_v1.xlsx (completed), encryption_key_flow_diagram.png, redlined_dpa_20270418.pdf.

DocuSign link (BlueFin signature): https://docusign.com/ABC-BlueFin-DPA-20270420

If helpful, happy to schedule a 30-minute call with Karthik to walk the diagram and custody choices.

Best regards,
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
T: +1-415-555-0173
E: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
